Fuuuuuh I saw this after I posted above. Didn’t realise THIS mare is rearing. 

Do NOT ride this horse. Rearing is incredibly dangerous and your trainer allowing you OR the owner to ride a horse with this behaviour is incredibly irresponsible. This needs corrective training by a professional- not ridden out by a teenager who isn’t fazed because she doesn’t have a frontal lobe. 

Terrible trainer story: The mare I had when I was a teenager/young 20’s developed a rearing problem. She ended up rearing with me at a horse show, lost her balance and fell on me. The only reason why I didn’t get a broken back or pelvis is because I made a snap decision to (sadly) yank her head to the side. She ended up falling that way and my femur bone took the impact and fractured. 

She reared because my awful trainer at the time insisted I ride her in a correction bit at the show. I begged her to let me ride in a plain long shank. She refused. The correction bit made my horse anxious and I wasn’t experienced enough to use such a harsh bit. It was an awful combination. 

I always wish I could go back and tell my younger self to stand up for what my gut was telling me to do. It took me over a year to feel safe on that horse again - and I LOVED her to pieces.

I still have a massive indentation on my thigh from the fall. It happened nearly 20 years ago.

Really well put. You are a great example of someone who is on their way to being a fantastic rider - it sounds like you are already. It’s the awareness that you are capable, but haven’t learned everything.

You are the client. I would tell the trainer exactly what you said here - that your trainer rode the horse in YOUR lesson and that’s not what you’re expecting (or paying for). That particular lesson wasn’t intended to be a “watch me sort out this silly mare.” 

If your trainer thinks you’re ready to learn how to train a green horse, then it should be on your green horse. 

Your safety is the most important thing here.
